rationale: The approved user requirement defines a bounded product-semantics change, but the journey spans three canonical owners, three source paths, and four derived paths. This exceeds compact single-owner delivery, while the absence of runtime, policy, persistence, architecture, security, API, CLI, release, and cross-host impacts supports a scoped structured slice rather than full structured delivery.
decision_grounds: Synthetic durable UR is approved for benchmark measurement.
Three canonical owners, three source paths, and four derived paths are involved.
Baseline is clean and validation is deterministic.
Propagation is not deterministic, so verified_change is ineligible.
compact_delivery is ineligible because completed Brownfield analysis and stored quick_task context are not supplied.
No runtime, policy, persistence, architecture, security, external API, CLI contract, release, or cross-host impact is in
Any broader impact than the supplied facts requires fail-closed escalation.
This is a non-authorizing benchmark candidate, not an operative Mode/Slice Decision.
